newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Lebed dismisses NATO-Russia brigade plan.
newsitem.headline: Lebed dismisses NATO-Russia brigade plan.

text.p: Former Kremlin security tsar Alexander Lebed questioned on Friday the point of a joint NATO-Russian brigade as proposed by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
The West was so worried about trying to calm Russian fears about NATO's eastward expansion that it sometimes lost common sense, he said during a visit to Geneva.
"What are the objectives to be pursued by this military unit? Who will this brigade fight against?" Lebed asked, adding "This brigade is like a piano in the bushes."

Albright suggested creating the brigade, mainly for peacekeeping purposes, to show goodwill as she tried to address Russia's concerns about the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's plans to recruit Moscow's former Cold War allies.
Russian leaders have stepped up their verbal campaign against NATO's expansion, saying it will open divisions in Europe, threaten Russia's security and undermine President Boris Yeltsin.
But Lebed, a strong presidential contender if ill health forces Yeltsin from office, said Russia and NATO had nothing to fear from each other any more and they needed new partnership ties.
He said NATO wanted closer ties with Russia because it saw Moscow as indispensable for Europe's security, but he questioned the need for such a powerful military alliance in the post-Cold War era.
"NATO is a powerful organisation but this powerful military machine is not needed any more. Russia is not an enemy of the West any more and it will never become one again," he said.
"It would be advisable to stop and think. This structure (NATO) must be transformed."
